'''William Alexander Lester Jr.''' (born April 24, 1937) is an American chemist who was a professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. He was awarded the [[National Organization for the Professional Advancement of Black Chemists and Chemical Engineers]] [[Percy L. Julian Award]], elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], and elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].

== Early life and education ==
Lester was born in the [[South Side, Chicago]], when schools were still segregated.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Lester |first=William A. Jr. |date=2007-03-19 |title=A Symposium in Honor of William A. Lester Jr. on His 70th Birthday |url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/1hb889x1 |language=en|journal=EScholarship}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Lester |first=William A. |date=2022-07-07 |title=From the South Side of Chicago to Berkeley, California with Stops in Between |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.jpca.2c03533 |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry A |language=en |volume=126 |issue=26 |pages=4123–4131 |doi=10.1021/acs.jpca.2c03533 |pmid=35708518 |bibcode=2022JPCA..126.4123L |s2cid=249711035 |issn=1089-5639|url-access=subscription }}</ref> After [[World War II]] his family moved and he enrolled at a high school that had previously been only for white people.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=William Lester Jr.'s Biography |url=https://www.thehistorymakers.org/biography/william-lester-jr |access-date=2022-08-13 |website=The HistoryMakers |language=en}}</ref> Lester secured a scholarship endowed by a former librarian from his [[Calumet High School (Chicago)|Calumet High School]], which allowed him to attend the [[University of Chicago]].<ref name=":1" />

Lester played college basketball. His sporting efforts are honored at the University of Chicago, where he is recognized as the first player to score over one thousand points, and the only player in UC history to average over twenty five points per game in a season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=William A. Lester, Jr. (2004) - Hall of Fame |url=https://athletics.uchicago.edu/honors/hall-of-fame/william-a-lester-jr-/76 |access-date=2025-06-29 |website=University of Chicago |language=en}}</ref>

He completed his bachelor's degree in chemistry, before which he had secured a part-time research position in the Laboratory of Molecular Structure and Spectra. The lab was based in the department of physics, which was directed by future Nobel laureate [[Robert S. Mulliken]].<ref name=":1" /> These interactions prompted him to focus on molecular quantum mechanics. He was supported by [[Henry Taube]] to pursue a master's degree, which he completed under the supervision of [[Stuart A. Rice]].<ref name=":1" />

At the [[Catholic University of America]] he carried out doctoral research on the molecular orbital structure of H<sub>3</sub>+.<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=A correlated molecular orbital study of the ground state of H<sub>3</sub>+ |date=1964 |language=English |first=William Alexander |last=Lester|oclc=47246106 }}</ref> During his studies, Lester became affiliated with the National Bureau of Standards— which later became the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]] (NIST)— where he spent nearly three years as a physical chemist.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2016-02-02 |title=Experiences of a Theoretical Chemist: Southside Chicago to Berkeley, California, with stops in-between |url=https://www.nist.gov/news-events/events/experiences-theoretical-chemist-southside-chicago-berkeley-california-stops |journal=NIST |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=2025-01-22 |title=African Americans in NIST History |url=https://www.nist.gov/history/african-americans-nist-history |journal=NIST |language=en}}</ref>

Lester had two children, including professional race car driver [[Bill Lester]].<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-2006-03-26-0603260268-story.html | title=Love of racing is in his blood | website=[[Chicago Tribune]] | date=26 March 2006 }}</ref>

== Research and career ==
In 1964, Lester joined the Theoretical Chemistry Institute at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], associated with the chemistry department, as a postdoctoral associate, soon after becoming its assistant director. After becoming an instructor on the Chemistry faculty, and working in Wisconsin for four years he attended an [[American Physical Society]] meeting at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], during which time he visited the [[IBM Research]] Lab.<ref name=":1" /> They offered him a position, and he joined Joseph Gayles there, but himself worked on atom-molecule inelastic scattering. In 1978, he was appointed Director of the National Resource for Computation in Chemistry, sited at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]. In 1983 he was made Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], and in 1991 he was elected Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=William A. Lester, Jr. {{!}} College of Chemistry |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/faculty/chem/lester |access-date=2022-08-12 |website=chemistry.berkeley.edu}}</ref>

Lester's research made use of computational chemistry to understand the electronic structures of molecules.<ref name=":1" /> He primarily used the [[Monte Carlo method]]. His group developed the matrix elements that connected various electronic states.<ref name=":1" />

== Awards and honors ==
* In 1957, Lester was awarded the University of Chicago Stagg Medal for scholarship, athletics and excellence of character.<ref name="Stagg">{{cite web |title=Amos Alonzo Stagg Medal Winners |url=https://athletics.uchicago.edu/sports/2023/6/12/stagg-medal.aspx |access-date=13 April 2025 |website=athletics.uchacogo.edu |publisher=University of Chicago}}</ref>
* In 1979, he received the [[Percy L. Julian Award]] of the [[National Organization for the Professional Advancement of Black Chemists and Chemical Engineers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 October 2021 |title=Dr. William Lester Jr. Featured in IAOTP's Top 50 Fearless Leaders Publication |url=https://www.prunderground.com/dr-william-lester-jr-featured-in-iaotps-top-50-fearless-leaders-publication/00244630/ |access-date=2022-08-13 |website=PRUnderground |language=en-US}}</ref> 
* In 1983, Lester was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], "For contributions to the application of computers to chemistry."<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellows Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship/dcp-fellowship |access-date=2025-06-29 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>
* In 2007, the [[University of California, Berkeley]] held a special symposium in honor of Lester's seventieth birthday.<ref name=":0" />
* In 2019 the Association of Top Professionals recognized Lester's distinguished career with a Lifetime Achievement Award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=William Lester: Lifetime achievement award {{!}} College of Chemistry |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/news/william-lester-lifetime-achievement-award |access-date=2022-08-13 |website=chemistry.berkeley.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor William Lester awarded lifetime achievement award {{!}} College of Chemistry |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/news/professor-william-lester-awarded-lifetime-achievement-award |access-date=2022-08-13 |website=chemistry.berkeley.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. William A. Lester Jr. |url=https://www.iaotp.com/drwilliamalesterjr |access-date=2022-08-13 |website=iaotp |language=en}}</ref>
* In 2020, the Chemistry Department at the University of California, Berkeley, established a lectureship in honor of Lester. The university stated, "The lectureship is intended to welcome distinguished underrepresented minority (URM) scholars to present their research and engage in discourse about their experiences and challenges of becoming scientists." In 2024, the lecturer was Mexican-American chemist [[Alán Aspuru-Guzik]], who had earned his doctoral degree under Lester's guidance.<ref name="Lectureship">{{cite web |title=The College of Chemistry Announces New Lectureship in Honor of William Lester |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/news/college-chemistry-announces-new-lectureship-honor-william-lester |website=chemistry.berkeley.edu |publisher=University of California |access-date=16 April 2025}}</ref><ref name="Lectureship2024">{{cite web |last1=Krol |first1=Melanie |title=Hispanic Heritage Month: Lester Lecture Speaker Alán Aspuru-Guzik |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/news/hispanic-heritage-month-lester-lecture-speaker-al%C3%A1n-aspuru-guzik |website=chemistry.berkeley.edu |publisher=University of California |access-date=17 April 2025}}</ref>
